messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Mutual Action Plan — load test milestone & capacity sizing (draft)

Thanks for taking time on the call this morning, Sam & Elena — good alignment overall. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the MAP milestone for the load/perf run.

Summary of the load test milestone (draft):
- Goal: validate peak QPS handling & latency SLOs for FinCloud production profile using traffic replay + scaled peak bursts.
- Scope: 2 replay slots (one peak, one off-peak) replaying ~2 weeks of representative traffic (sampled logs) scaled to target peak QPS.
- Redwood deliverables: traffic replay orchestration, dedicated capacity sizing recommendation, runbook, test-day monitoring + tracing capture.
- FinCloud deliverables: sample logs (S3 link or paste), PII redaction confirmation, test POC for calendar coordination and account/procurement contact for capacity commit.

Proposed milestone owners & target dates (editable in the attached MAP):
- Finalize MAP draft (owner: Lauren) — target: 2026-05-21
- Capacity sizing & instance recommendation (owner: Karthik) — target: 2026-05-20
- Schedule replay windows (owner: Marissa + FinCloud POC) — proposed windows below
- Test execution & runbook signoff (owner: joint) — target: week of 2026-06-21
- Target close (signature/procurement): 2026-06-30 (flexible)

Redwood recommended test windows (US/Eastern framing for scheduling):
- Peak window: 2026-06-24 09:00–11:00 EDT (primary)
- Backfill/off-peak window: 2026-06-24 20:00–22:00 EDT (secondary)

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm whether the June 24 windows work (or propose alternatives within Jun 22–26).
2) Share a sample of 48–72 hours of production logs (S3 or Transfer link) and a single-row summary of current peak QPS and burst QPS.
3) Point me to the procurement/Security contact for SOC/SLA paperwork we should route towards.

Attached: MAP-draft-FinCloud-v1.xlsx (editable) and traffic-replay-specs.pdf (technical checklist). I’ll iterate after we get your log sample and preferred windows.

—
Lauren Bishop | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Sam’s note and the MAP draft. Please see the asks above; callout items below that I want included in the formal MAP before I send back to FinCloud.

Callouts (to turn into MAP rows):
- Capacity recommendation: we need a quick run of synthetic peak-scaling estimates and an initial Reserved vs Burst cost delta so FinCloud can see order-of-magnitude spend before committing.
- KV-cache and model variant: they’ll need guidance on whether we keep single-model baseline vs a fallback smaller quantized variant for burst periods (affects instance count).
- Monitoring hooks: Marissa, please prepare the minimal set of dashboards (latency p95/p99, per-token cost, GPU mem/cpu, kv-hit ratio) we’ll expose on test day.
- Logistics: I’ll ask them for the S3 link — once logs arrive, Karthik, can you run the quick estimator and drop notes in the MAP spreadsheet?

Attachments included in this thread: MAP-draft-FinCloud-v1.xlsx, traffic-replay-specs.pdf (both attached here). Also adding a DocuSign stub in the related links for procurement flow.

Next internal step: Karthik — can you produce a sizing recommendation and suggested autoscale policy by EOD tomorrow (2026-05-19)? I’ll then push the updated MAP to Sam and Elena.

—
Lauren
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — load test milestone & capacity sizing (draft)

Lauren — thanks, looping through my quick sizing notes below; I’ll formalize in the MAP spreadsheet (row: Capacity Sizing) and attach an estimator snapshot.

High-level recommendation (initial):
- Baseline: 3 x NVIDIA A100 80GB reserved nodes (sustained traffic handling ~8–10k qps depending on batching).
- Peak/burst: Autoscale policy to allow burst up to 6 GPUs (A100 or H100 equivalent) for short 30–60s spikes — this addresses the 18k qps bursts Sam called out.
- Alternative compact option (lower cost, slightly higher latency): use 6 x T4/RTX-class quantized variant nodes for fallback when strict latency SLOs can be relaxed.

Estimated perf/obs:
- With optimized continuous batching and KV prefix cache hit ≥70%, the A100 pool above should maintain p95 latency within target for the sampled payloads.
- If we need sub-100ms p50 guarantees at peak, we should consider 4x A100s reserved + burst to 8x for the busiest 60s windows.

Proposed MAP milestone updates (I’ll add these as rows):
- Capacity sizing recommendation: Karthik (owner) — 2026-05-19
- Cost delta snapshot (Reserved vs Burst): Karthik & Lauren — 2026-05-20
- Confirm test windows & calendar invites: Marissa & FinCloud POC — 2026-05-21

Proposed test windows (confirming Lauren’s suggestion):
- 2026-06-24 09:00–11:00 EDT (peak replay)
- 2026-06-24 20:00–22:00 EDT (off-peak replay)

Next steps I’ll take now:
1) Run the quick estimator on the 72-hr sample once Sam shares S3 link.
2) Drop an editable sizing table in the MAP-draft-FinCloud-v1.xlsx with GPU counts and approximate cost ranges.
3) Sync with Marissa for the monitoring dashboard checklist and the runbook play-by-play.

If we agree on the above, I’m happy to present the sizing section during the next customer sync or a dedicated 30-min technical call.

—
